title: Ex 2.5 #1 · Truth table for P ∨ (Q ⇒ R)
prompt: Build a truth table for $P \vee (Q \Rightarrow R)$ and enter the truth value of the whole statement in each row.
answer_format: Eight T/F values, one per row, top to bottom, like T T F T T F T T. Rows (P, Q, R) go TTT, TTF, TFT, TFF, FTT, FTF, FFT, FFF, as in the book. Helper columns are optional steps, like ~P : F F F F T T T T.
answer: T T T T T F T T
hints: Start with a helper column for Q ⇒ R. It is false only in the rows where Q is true and R is false.
An ∨ statement is true as soon as one side is true, so every row where P is true gets T.
solution: The helper column for $Q \Rightarrow R$ is T F T T T F T T: it is false only when $Q$ is true and $R$ is false.
In the top four rows $P$ is true, so $P \vee (Q \Rightarrow R)$ is true there. In the bottom four rows it matches $Q \Rightarrow R$.
So the column is T T T T T F T T.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).

submission.answer: T T T T T F T T
